conventionApplied: Only PRESENT-TENSE state assertions are flagged. _sessions/* and dated point-in-time paragraphs inside _STATE.md that are explicitly scoped to a past date are treated as HISTORICAL RECORDS and are NOT flagged for correction. _STATE.md's undated 'LIVE NUMBERS' section IS flagged because it asserts present-tense state. _decisions/* are treated as RULINGS: their reasoning-as-of-date is historical, but a criterion stated in the imperative ('the gate is X') is present-tense and IS flagged.

atomFindings: CONFIRMED ALIGNED — accessPolicy. The published @empressaio/atom-contract@1.19.0 declares the five-value union at dist/registration.d.ts:48: 'public-free' | 'public-paid' | 'platform-internal' | 'tenant-private' | 'tenant-shared'. This matches CLAUDE.md and 01a_atom_conventions.md exactly. No correction needed.

CONFIRMED ALIGNED — conformance target. ATOM_CONFORMANCE_TARGET_VERSION is literally '1.5.0' in the published 1.19.0 tarball (dist/conformance/common.d.ts:14). 01a_atom_conventions.md and 25_atom_architecture_reference.md are both CORRECT to say 1.5.0.

GAP — two conformance targets are undocumented anywhere in doc_repo. The published contract also declares REASONING_CONFORMANCE_TARGET_VERSION = '1.8.0' (common.d.ts:20) and PROPERTY_CONFORMANCE_TARGET_VERSION = '1.15.0' (common.d.ts:25). The property target is the one that actually governs the county rails, and no canonical doc mentions it. An agent told 'the conformance target is 1.5.0' will validate property atoms against the wrong target.

MISMATCH — PACKAGE NAME. 25_atom_architecture_reference.md is status:active, is titled '@hauska/atom-contract — Architecture reference', and uses the retired name in at least 12 places including the package-surface spec. CLAUDE.md says that name 'appears in historical records only'. This doc is not a historical record; it is the named authority for the substrate contract.

MISMATCH — REGISTERED FAMILIES. hauska-engine origin/main (tip 34c94ff) PROPERTY_ENTITY_TYPES has 14 members: parcel-node, zoning-fact, setback-rule, buildable-envelope, parcel-terrain-model, building-footprint, utility-easement, flood-hazard-fact, cad-parcel-roll, land-use-fact, owner-fact, rail-corridor-fact, well-fact, special-district-fact. NO doc_repo canonical doc enumerates this list. 01a_atom_conventions.md and _catalog/atoms_index.md cover only the portfolio-atom layer; 25_atom_architecture_reference.md predates every one of these families.

STRUCTURAL GAP — road-node IS PUBLISHED BUT NOT REGISTERED. The contract 1.19.0 ships dist/property/road-node.{d.ts,js} with entityType 'road-node', a full ROAD_NODE_SCHEMA, road classification enum, ROW provenance and attach points — exported from the ./property barrel (index.d.ts:16). The engine does NOT include road-node in PROPERTY_ENTITY_TYPES. Five documents each hold a PIECE of the definition and no document holds all of it, none of them agree on the denominator, and the one that comes closest is not gradable. (3) 90_operations/OPS-WDLL_the_factory.md holds a genuine WDLL with done/broken/kill criteria, but it is scoped to the FACTORY as a machine at the JURISDICTION grain, was written 2026-08-03 before the layer-first pivot, and its status section still reads 'Bastrop city, mid-warm'. (4) _inbox/2026-08-09_W1_writers_program_WDLL.md is a real gradable card with 15 acceptance items — the ONLY properly-shaped WDLL in the program — but it covers one workstream, carries the wrong rail count, and every grade box is still empty. (5) _STATE.md holds the live state and is the only doc an agent actually reads, but it is unratified, CLAUDE.md does not mention it, and its own LIVE NUMBERS section is wrong. RECOMMENDATION: make OPS-14 canonical and give it what it lacks — a DEFINITION OF DONE section that restates the six amended gate criteria as gradable rows in the W1 WDLL's shape (claim | instrument | live reading | grade), each naming the query or endpoint that grades it. THE GATE'S ARITHMETIC WAS OBSOLETE WITHIN 24 HOURS OF BEING RULED, AND IT WAS PREDICTED. OPS-15 line 187 warned in writing that splitting rails immediately before a gate defined as 'all rails with writers' makes the gate harder by definition. The split was ruled the next day and applied the day after. The gate was never amended. The warning was recorded, ignored in the sense that nobody amended the gate, and is now the top blocker to grading the program. The lesson worth capturing: a gate expressed as a COUNT of a dimension that is still being edited will rot; the gate should have been expressed over the dimension ('every rail in county_rail') rather than over its cardinality ('all 12 rails').
